title: How big is the biggest star?

narration.heading: Biggest star?
narration.text: You think the Sun is huge? Wait till you see what's sitting next to it.

narration.heading: The Moon
narration.text: Start with the Moon, about three and a half thousand kilometres across. Now here comes Earth.

narration.heading: Earth
narration.text: Earth is almost four Moons wide, at twelve thousand seven hundred kilometres.

narration.heading: Jupiter
narration.text: Next, Jupiter. If it were hollow, about a thousand Earths would fit inside.

narration.heading: The Sun
narration.text: The Sun makes Jupiter look tiny. One point three million Earths could fill it.

narration.heading: Betelgeuse
narration.text: Then Betelgeuse, the red shoulder of Orion, about seven hundred and sixty times wider than the Sun.

narration.heading: The twist
narration.text: Put it where the Sun is, and its surface would reach past Mars. You'd be living inside a star.

narration.heading: UY Scuti
narration.text: And UY Scuti is bigger still, about nine hundred Suns wide. Seven hundred and fifty million Suns would fit inside.

narration.heading: Even bigger?
narration.text: And it might not even be the biggest. What's the biggest thing you can imagine?

hook.banner: How big is the biggest star?

skit.text: Nine hundred Suns? And I complain when my fan gets warm.

titles: How big is the biggest star? (it's not the Sun)
From the Moon to UY Scuti, to scale
youtube.description: A to-scale zoom out from the Moon to Earth, Jupiter, the Sun, Betelgeuse and UY Scuti, one of the largest known stars: about 909 times wider than the Sun.

sources.claim: The Moon is about 3,475 km across
Jupiter's radius is 69,911 km; about 1,000 Earths would fit inside it
The Sun is about 1.4 million km wide; about 1.3 million Earths would fill it
Betelgeuse's radius is about 764 solar radii (Joyce et al. 2020); at the Sun's position it would engulf the orbits of Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars
Mars orbits at about 1.52 AU (so its orbit is about 456 million km across)
UY Scuti's radius is about 909 solar radii (2023); its volume is about 750 million times the Sun's; it may not be the largest known star
